hints: Because both sides of the inequality are non-negative, square them to remove the modulus signs.
Move all terms to one side and factor the resulting quadratic expression.
Use the two linear factors to find the critical values of $x$.
Construct a sign chart and use the strict greater-than sign to select the two exterior intervals with excluded endpoints.
walkthrough:
Square both sides of the inequality $3|2x - 1| > |x + 4|$ since both sides are non-negative:
$$(3|2x - 1|)^2 > (|x + 4|)^2$$
$$9(2x - 1)^2 > (x + 4)^2$$

Collect all terms on the left side to form a quadratic inequality:
$$(36 - 1)x^2 + (-36 - 8)x + (9 - 16) > 0$$
$$35x^2 - 44x - 7 > 0$$

Find the roots of the corresponding equation $35x^2 - 44x - 7 = 0$ by factoring:
$$(5x - 7)(7x + 1) = 0$$
$$5x - 7 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{7}{5}$$
$$7x + 1 = 0 \implies x = -\dfrac{1}{7}$$

Because the quadratic coefficient is positive ($35 > 0$), the expression is positive strictly outside the interval between the roots:
$$x > \dfrac{7}{5} \quad \text{or} \quad x < -\dfrac{1}{7}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Modulus Equations and Inequaliti: Identifies non-modular inequality $3^2(2x-1)^2>(x+4)^2$, or corresponding quadratic equation, or pair of linear equations/inequalities $3(2x-1)=\pm(x+4)$; Derives critical values $x=\dfrac75$ and $x=-\dfrac17$; Concludes with $x>\dfrac75$ or $x<-\dfrac17$.
